stem_ctx:
A program is being developed to control a simple alarm system to be used in a house. The alarm
    has a control panel with a keypad and a screen to display text.
    The keypad consists of 36 character keys:
    •   26 upper‑case letter keys, allowing A to Z to be entered
    •   10 digit keys, allowing 0 to 9 to be entered.

When the alarm system is initially installed, a password must be created. When the
        password is initially entered, it is checked to ensure that it follows a set of validation rules. It
        is then permanently stored in the alarm system.
        For a password to be valid it must follow these validation rules:
        Rule 1: contain between six and eight characters inclusive.
        Rule 2: contain at least one letter and one digit.
        Rule 3: each character can only occur once.
        The global variable Pass is used to store the password entered.
ms_text: STRING

stem_ctx:
A programmer has defined a global 1D array Numbers of type INTEGER, which can store 1000
    integers. The lower bound of the array Numbers is set to 1. Each element of the array has been
    initialised with a random integer in the range 200 to 99 999.
    The programmer has written a bubble sort algorithm to sort the array Numbers into
    ascending order.
    Study algorithm A.
    Assume all the variables have been correctly declared.
    algorithm A:
    FOR LoopCounter     1 TO 999                    //Outer Loop
        FOR Index     1 TO 999                        //Inner Loop
           IF Numbers[Index] > Numbers[Index + 1] THEN
               //Start of block to swap neighbouring elements in the array
               Temp     Numbers[Index]
               Numbers[Index]     Numbers[Index + 1]
               Numbers[Index + 1]     Temp
               //End of block to swap neighbouring elements in the array
           ENDIF
        NEXT Index
    NEXT LoopCounter
ms_text:
The greater than logic operator / >  in the selection statement
 would need to be changed to a less than operator / <
 Or by example
 IF Numbers[Index] > Numbers[Index + 1] THEN
 would be changed to
 IF Numbers[Index] < Numbers[Index + 1] THEN
 OR
 IF Numbers[Index] <= Numbers[Index + 1] THEN
 OR
 IF Numbers[Index + 1] >  Numbers[Index] THEN
 OR
 IF Numbers[Index + 1] >=  Numbers[Index] THEN
tag_note: 按题干产出及指南 §2、§7 定主题型；副题型按 §4 阈值。

stem_ctx:
A programmer has defined a global 1D array Numbers of type INTEGER, which can store 1000
    integers. The lower bound of the array Numbers is set to 1. Each element of the array has been
    initialised with a random integer in the range 200 to 99 999.
    The programmer has written a bubble sort algorithm to sort the array Numbers into
    ascending order.
    Study algorithm A.
    Assume all the variables have been correctly declared.
    algorithm A:
    FOR LoopCounter     1 TO 999                    //Outer Loop
        FOR Index     1 TO 999                        //Inner Loop
           IF Numbers[Index] > Numbers[Index + 1] THEN
               //Start of block to swap neighbouring elements in the array
               Temp     Numbers[Index]
               Numbers[Index]     Numbers[Index + 1]
               Numbers[Index + 1]     Temp
               //End of block to swap neighbouring elements in the array
           ENDIF
        NEXT Index
    NEXT LoopCounter

The programmer rewrites the bubble sort algorithm to make it more efficient.
        Study algorithm B.
        Assume all the variables have been correctly declared.
        algorithm B:
        Boundary     999
        REPEAT                                     //Outer Loop
            NoSwaps     TRUE
            FOR Index     1 TO Boundary          //Inner Loop
               IF Numbers[Index] > Numbers[Index + 1] THEN
                   //Start of block to swap neighbouring elements in the array
                   Temp     Numbers[Index]
                   Numbers[Index]     Numbers[Index + 1]
                   Numbers[Index + 1]     Temp
                   //End of block to swap neighbouring elements in the array
                   NoSwaps     FALSE
               ENDIF
            NEXT Index
            Boundary     Boundary ‑ 1
        UNTIL NoSwaps = TRUE
ms_text:
2 marks for inner loop
 MP 1: The inner loop iterates one less time (in algorithm B)
 each time the outer / repeat loop iterates.
 MP 2: this is because for each iteration of the outer / repeat
 loop (in algorithm B) the last / one more element in the
 Numbers array will be in the correct place.
 2 marks for outer loop
 MP 3: The outer / repeat loop (in algorithm B) would stop
 iterating if no swaps are made / all numbers in array are sorted
 MP 4: so not as many iterations would be needed (if the
 Numbers array is not initially sorted)
tag_note: 按题干产出及指南 §2、§7 定主题型；副题型按 §4 阈值。

    initialised with a random integer in the range 200 to 99 999.
    The programmer has written a bubble sort algorithm to sort the array Numbers into
    ascending order.
    Study algorithm A.
    Assume all the variables have been correctly declared.
    algorithm A:
    FOR LoopCounter     1 TO 999                    //Outer Loop
        FOR Index     1 TO 999                        //Inner Loop
           IF Numbers[Index] > Numbers[Index + 1] THEN
               //Start of block to swap neighbouring elements in the array
               Temp     Numbers[Index]
               Numbers[Index]     Numbers[Index + 1]
               Numbers[Index + 1]     Temp
               //End of block to swap neighbouring elements in the array
           ENDIF
        NEXT Index
    NEXT LoopCounter

          PROCEDURE Swap(Num1 : INTEGER, Num2 : INTEGER)
              DECLARE Temp : INTEGER
              Temp     Num1
              Num1     Num2
              Num2     Temp
          ENDPROCEDURE
        The programmer replaces the block of pseudocode in the algorithm that swaps the values in
        two neighbouring elements in the array with a call to this procedure.
        The block of code:
          Temp     Numbers[Index]
          Numbers[Index]     Numbers[Index + 1]
          Numbers[Index + 1]     Temp

A program is being developed to encrypt a message.
    The following terms are used in the encryption technique to be used:
            term                                  definition
     plain text            The original message before it is encrypted.
     cipher text           The encrypted version of the plain text.
    The encryption method to be used is based on the algorithm for the Caesar Box Cipher. All plain
    text messages to be encrypted must be 25 characters in length or less. If a message is less than
    25 characters in length, then spaces are added to the end to make the padded plain text the
    required length.
    A square grid of five columns and five rows is used. The padded plain text message is put into
    the grid row by row. The cipher text is obtained by reading the grid column by column.
    For example:
        plain text: This is a message
        The number of characters in the original plain text, including spaces, is 17.
        plain text with added spaces at the end: This∆is∆a∆message∆∆∆∆∆∆∆∆
        The character ∆ is used to indicate a space in the padded plain text.
        The grid filled, row by row, with the padded plain text.
           T     h     i     s     ∆
           i     s     ∆     a     ∆
           m     e     s     s     a
           g     e     ∆     ∆     ∆
           ∆     ∆     ∆     ∆     ∆
        The cipher text is obtained by reading the grid column by column.
        cipher text: Timg∆hsee∆i∆s∆∆sas∆∆∆∆a∆∆
    The programmer has defined the first program module as:
          module                                 description
                        •   user prompt for and input of plain text
                        •   check plain text contains between 1 and 25 characters inclusive
                        •   re‑input of plain text until it contains between 1 and 25 characters
     AddPadding()
                        •   if required, additional space characters are added to the end of
                            the plain text to ensure it contains exactly 25 characters
                        •   return of amended plain text
ms_text:
Mark Schme One – loop used to form return string
 (See MS Two for solutions using LEFT()/MID() to form
 return string)
 Example solution
 FUNCTION AddPadding() RETURNS STRING
     CONSTANT Space = ' '
     DECLARE Plaintext : STRING
     DECLARE LenOfPlaintext : INTEGER
     DECLARE Index : INTEGER
     REPEAT
         OUTPUT "Enter plaintext"
         INPUT Plaintext
         LenOfPlaintext  LENGTH(Plaintext)
     UNTIL LenOfPlaintext >= 1 AND LenOfPlaintext
 <= 25
     FOR Index  LenOfPlaintext + 1 TO 25
         Plaintext  Plaintext & Space
     NEXT Index
     // Alternative way to append spaces using
 while loop
     WHILE LENGTH(Plaintext) <> 25
         Plaintext  Plaintext & Space
     ENDWHILE
     //Alternative way to append spaces
     DECLARE SpaceString : STRING
     SpaceString  ""
     FOR Index  LenOfPlaintext + 1 TO 25
         SpaceString  SpaceString & Space
     NEXT Index
     Plaintext  Plaintext & SpaceString
     RETURN Plaintext
 ENDFUNCTION
 Mark points
 1   Function heading, return type and ending
 2   Prompt for and input of plaintext
 3   Conditional loop that checks one of the boundary values
 4   Conditional loop that correctly checks both boundaries of
 plaintext
 5   …Re-input of plaintext in a loop
 6   Loop that iterates for number of spaces to add to end of
 plaintext
 7   …Spaces appended to plaintext // Spaces appended to an
 empty string
 8   Correctly padded plaintext returned following a reasonable
 attempt at MP7
 Mark Scheme Two - No Loop used to form return string –
 use of LEFT()/MID() Function
 Example Solution:
 FUNCTION AddPadding() RETURNS STRING
     CONSTANT Fill = "                        " //24
 Spaces

         INPUT Plaintext
         LenOfPlaintext  LENGTH(Plaintext)
     UNTIL LenOfPlaintext >= 1 AND LenOfPlaintext
 <= 25
     Plaintext  LEFT(Plaintext & Fill, 25)
     RETURN Plaintext
 ENDFUNCTION

 3   Conditional loop that checks one of the boundary values
     Conditional loop that correctly checks for length of plaintext
 4   …Re-input of plaintext in a loop

     Correct use of LEFT() / MID() function and & to append
     padding characters

     attempt at
     MP 6 and MP 7

Solution One : Using nested loop and output of each row in a
 loop following nested loop
 Example Solution
 PROCEDURE PopulateGrid(Plaintext : STRING)
     DECLARE Row, Column, Index : INTEGER
     Index  1
     FOR Row  1 TO 5
         FOR Column  1 TO 5
            Grid[Row, Column]  MID(Plaintext,
 Index, 1)
            Index  Index + 1
         NEXT Column
     Next Row
     FOR Row  1 TO 5
         OUTPUT Grid[Row, 1], Grid[Row, 2],
 Grid[Row, 3],_
                                     Grid[Row, 4],
 Grid[Row, 5]
     NEXT Row
 ENDPROCEDURE

 Solution Two: Using nested loop and output of each string in a
 loop following nested loop -
 Example Solution
 PROCEDURE PopulateGrid(Plaintext : STRING)
     DECLARE Row, Column, Index : INTEGER
     DECLARE RowString : STRING
     FOR Row  1 TO 5
         FOR Column  1 TO 5
            Index  (Row – 1) * 5 + Column
            Grid[Row, Column]  MID(Plaintext,
 Index, 1)
         NEXT Column
     NEXT Row
     FOR Row  1 TO 5
         RowString ""
         For Col  1 TO 5

 Column]

     NEXT Row
